important.name: Pinned catalog schema copies reject the keyword inbox put now requires
important.summary: `inbox put` now refuses any item without `keyword` (inbox.py:141 -> keywords.require_keywords) and validates against the harness schema, but rule T1 validates the catalog against the project's pinned copy (`<todo.folder>/RepoToDo.schema.json`, the `todo.catalog_schema` default, rules_todo.py:33-36), whose closed `$defs/item` predates `keyword`. In such a project every item queued by /harness:add-todo or /harness:sync-gh-todo after the upgrade drains into a catalog its own schema rejects (T1 error), and `todo_sync.py keywords` does the same to every item it fills. The only warning lives in the release note (docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:330); the root README's TODO section, which carries the equivalent warning for migrate-ids (README.md:498-501), and todo_sync.md's `inbox put`/`keywords` sections say nothing, and nothing at runtime notices the stale copy.
fix: Guard it: have `require_keywords` (or `inbox.put`) and `apply_keywords` check the project's `todo.catalog_schema` and, when its `$defs/item.properties` lacks `keyword`, refuse with a problem line telling the project to refresh its copy from catalogs/TodoCatalog.schema.json (or skip the requirement until it does).

At minimum document it where consumers look: add a sentence to README.md's TODO section next to the migrate-ids schema-copy advice and to plugins/harness/scripts/todo_sync.md's `inbox put` and `keywords` sections: update the project's pinned RepoToDo.schema.json before the first keyworded item lands.

important.name: valid_keyword accepts a trailing newline, which then breaks the one-line status
important.summary:
KEYWORD_RE is anchored with `$` and applied with `.match`, and Python's `$` also matches just before a final newline. So valid_keyword('banner
') returns True, and so does the reshape `keyword` type rule (verified). The jsonschema item check that `_check_item` runs also accepts it, because Python's jsonschema uses `re.search` with the same `$`. An `add` or `inbox put` spec with "keyword": "banner
" therefore passes every gate and lands in the catalog. The contract is one word of letters, digits, '_', '.' or '-'. On the TypeScript side, `keywordsIn` (hide.ts) accepts any non-empty string, so the newline reaches the `line` atom, line.txt and line.json and splits the single status line in two.

Also (adv_code_runtime): valid_keyword checks with KEYWORD_RE.match and a pattern ending in `$`. In Python, `$` also matches just before a final newline, so 'stop_gates
' counts as valid. Every gate on the add, inbox put and update paths relies on this check: require_keywords (any non-blank string), the reshape `keyword` type rule (`_text(v) and keywords.valid_keyword(v)`) and the catalog schema check. Python jsonschema runs the pattern with re.search, so it has the same `$` behavior and also lets the value through. The value reaches the catalog unchanged. hide.ts keywordsIn takes any non-empty string, and line.ts labelText puts it straight into the plain line, line.json and the ccstatusline text. The single-line working line then gets a line break in the middle of a label, and fitCount measures a string that contains a newline.

Attack: Probe run at the PR head: `keywords.valid_keyword('stop_gates
')` returns True; `reshape._TYPE_RULES['keyword'][0]('stop_gates
')` returns True; and `jsonschema.Draft202012Validator({'type':'string','pattern':'^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$','maxLength':32}).iter_errors('stop_gates
')` gives no errors. End to end: `todo_sync.py inbox put --spec s.json` with an item that is otherwise valid and has `"keyword": "stop_gates
"` is queued without complaint, and `add --inbox` writes it to the catalog (`inbox put --update` with `{"fields": {"keyword": "stop_gates
"}}` does the same). After that, `buildLine` with `view.keywords` = keywordsOf(catalog) gives a `text` containing 'todo-xxxx stop_gates
', and statusText splits the working line in two. A unit test asserting `not valid_keyword('a
')` fails today.

Also (adv_code_tests): The keyword tests claim a value that is not one word is refused, but none tries a trailing newline. `KEYWORD_RE` (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, used through `re.match`) lets `$` match before a final `
`, and the Python `jsonschema` validator applies the schema pattern with `re.search`, so it has the same hole. `"parser
"` therefore passes `valid_keyword`, `has_keyword`, the `reshape` `_TYPE_RULES["keyword"]` check behind `inbox put` / `add --spec` / `update`, and the catalog schema (rule T1). The working-refs mod then reads it as-is (`hide.ts` `keywordsIn` takes any non-empty string), so the label `todo-xxxx parser
` puts a line break into the `line` atom, `line.txt` and `line.json`. An ECMA-262 validator would refuse the same catalog, so the Python and JS sides also disagree.

Attack: Probe run at the PR head (with harness_lib on sys.path): `keywords.valid_keyword('parser
')` -> True; `keywords.has_keyword({'keyword': 'parser
'})` -> True; `reshape._TYPE_RULES['keyword'][0]('parser
')` -> True; `jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(schema['$defs']['item']['properties']['keyword']).iter_errors('parser
')` -> [] (no errors). End to end: `todo_sync.py inbox put --spec s.json` where s.json is `{"items":[{...valid item..., "keyword": "parser
"}]}` queues the item with no refusal. After the drain, the catalog passes T1. The working-refs `keywordsOf` maps the id to `'parser
'`, and `buildLine` returns text `todo-xxxx parser
` with a newline inside it. Adding `"parser
"` to the parametrize list at tests/schemas/test_todo_keyword_schema.py:41 makes `test_a_keyword_that_is_not_one_word_is_refused_by_its_pattern` fail, because the validator set is empty.
fix: In keywords.valid_keyword use `KEYWORD_RE.fullmatch(value)`, or anchor the pattern with `\Z` instead of `$`. The reshape rule at reshape.py:192 and require_keywords both inherit the fix.
Also have hide.ts keywordsIn keep only keywords that match /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,31}$/, so a hand-edited catalog cannot put control characters into the terminal line.

In keywords.py valid_keyword, use `KEYWORD_RE.fullmatch(value)`, or end KEYWORD_RE with `\Z` instead of `$`, so 'stop_gates\n' is refused on every path that calls the reshape type rule (add, inbox put, inbox put --update).

Also, in hide.ts keywordsIn, keep a keyword only when it matches /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$/ (in JS, `$` without the m flag does not match before a newline) and has at most 32 characters, so a hand-edited checked-out catalog cannot inject line breaks or escape sequences into the status line.

In `plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/keywords.py:25-43`, use `KEYWORD_RE.fullmatch(value)` (or end the regex with `\Z`). Add `"parser\n"` to the refused cases in `tests/schemas/test_todo_keyword_schema.py:41` and to a put test in `tests/lib/test_todo_sync_keyword_put.py`.

Also make the mod's `keywordsIn` (`plugins/working-refs/hooks/hide.ts`) keep a keyword only when it matches `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,31}$/`, and add a `keywordsOf` case in `hide.test.ts:28-36` with `keyword: 'a\nb'` and one with an ESC byte, both skipped.

minor.name: sync step 3 leaves keyword out of the keys each item carries
minor.summary:
todo-editor.md sync step 3 lists the keys each item carries (lines 181-184): issue, url, title, kind, ..., why_ranked, with optional keys after them. `keyword` appears only in the shapes sentence that follows. **add** step 3 says `keyword` is included, and `inbox put` now refuses an item without one. minor.name: Sync step 4 treats a keyword refusal as one item, but a spec can lack several
minor.summary: plugins/harness/agents/todo-editor.md:199-200 says a `lacks keyword` problem line "is that one rerun: set the keyword from the suggestion and put again" (add step 3 at line 235 repeats it). keywords.require_keywords (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/keywords.py:163-168) raises on the first spec item without a keyword only. A sync spec drafts one item per issue, so with two or more keywordless items the agent fixes the named one, the rerun refuses the next, and the run hits the stop condition after its single allowed rerun.
fix: Reword the prose: on a `lacks keyword` refusal, rerun `TS suggest-keyword --spec <path>` and set `keyword` on every item that lacks one before the one rerun.
Or have require_keywords collect every keywordless item into one refusal (one `item <n> lacks keyword (...)` clause per item) so a single fix covers them all; update todo_sync.md:193-197 to match.

minor.name: The 'high confidence' guesser labels three unrelated items PROVENANCE
minor.summary:
GENERIC_STEMS skips SKILL and README but not shared index docs, so any item whose files lean on docs/PROVENANCE.md gets that stem as its 'confident' keyword. The committed migration output shows it: todo items at RepoToDo.json:95 (post-forcepush Step 6), :3108 (port test-driven-development) and :3910 (diagnosing-superpowers decision) all read `PROVENANCE`, and :3691/:3964 share `pr_review_skill_description` for two different skill decisions. A label meant to jog memory that is identical across unrelated items jogs nothing, and `inbox put` will now suggest the same word to the agent.

Also (system_shape): The one-time `keywords` run gave three unrelated items the keyword `PROVENANCE` (RepoToDo.json:95, 3108, 3910), two `pr_review_skill_description` (3691, 3964) and two `HARNESS_RULES` (2523, 2582): the files-dominance guess picked a shared bookkeeping doc rather than the subject. The schema describes the keyword as 'the one word that jogs a reader's memory of the item', which a label shared by unrelated TODOs does not do on the working line.
fix: Add `PROVENANCE` (and any similar shared index stem, e.g. `CHANGELOG`) to GENERIC_STEMS in keywords.py, add a `generic-only` style test case for it, then hand-fix or `inbox put --update` the five catalog items with real subject words.
Leave the guesser alone and replace the five keywords in docs/TODO/RepoToDo.json by hand with words that name each item's subject.
Hand-correct those catalog keywords (e.g. post-forcepush, test-driven-development, diagnosing-superpowers) through `inbox put --update`.
Or tighten `_files_guess`: skip `.md` stems that are ALL-CAPS shared docs, or require the dominant stem to be a code file, without naming project files in the plugin.

minor.name: Keyword refusal names only the first item, but the agent gets one rerun
minor.summary: require_keywords raises on the first spec item lacking a keyword (keywords.py:163-168), so a multi-item sync spec with several gaps is refused one item at a time. todo-editor.md sync step 4 says a `lacks keyword` problem 'is that one rerun: set the keyword from the suggestion and put again', so an agent that fixes only the named item hits a second refusal with its rerun budget spent and leaves the spec unqueued. The doc contract and the refusal granularity do not fit together.
fix: Make require_keywords collect every lacking item into one TodoSyncError (`item 2 lacks keyword (suggested: X); item 4 lacks keyword (...)`) and update the todo_sync.md `inbox put` paragraph to match.
Or reword todo-editor.md step 4: on a `lacks keyword` refusal run `suggest-keyword` again and set `keyword` on every item that lacks one before the rerun.

minor.name: The keyword type-rule message omits the leading-character rule
minor.summary: The _TYPE_RULES entry for `keyword` (reshape.py:192-193) refuses a value that fails keywords.valid_keyword, which requires the first character to be a letter or digit (KEYWORD_RE). Its message says only "one word of letters, digits, '_', '.' or '-' (at most 32 characters)". The agent therefore sees `-x` or `_x` refused with text those values appear to satisfy.
fix: Change the message to "one word of letters, digits, '_', '.' or '-', starting with a letter or digit (at most {keywords.KEYWORD_MAX} characters)".

minor.name: An update that sets keyword appends it at the item's end, not after the title
minor.summary:
The release note says `add --spec`, the inbox drain and `inbox put --update` keep the keyword right after the title. The add path (reshape._item_fields) and the migration (keywords._with_keyword) do. The update path does not. updates._apply_one lays fields with `item.update(...)` (updates.py:84), so an item that had no keyword gets `keyword` as its last key. The only update test, test_an_update_may_set_the_keyword (test_todo_sync_keyword_put.py:93-94), checks that 'keyword' is in UPDATE_FIELDS and never runs apply_updates. Nothing pins what an update actually writes.

Also (roast): updates._apply_one lays fields over the item with `item.update(...)`, so an update giving a keyword-less item its first keyword puts `keyword` after `related_gh_issues`/`priority`, not right after `title` as `_item_fields` and `fill_keywords` do. The release note at docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:329 says `inbox put --update` keeps it right after the title. The only update test, test_an_update_may_set_the_keyword, asserts `'keyword' in UPDATE_FIELDS` - a constant lookup that cannot see placement.

Also (docs, system_shape): docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:329 says `add --spec`, the inbox drain and `inbox put --update` accept a keyword "and keep it right after the title". That holds for the add path (reshape._item_fields inserts it after `title`), but an update goes through updates._apply_one (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/updates.py:84), which does `item.update(fields)`: an update that gives a keyword to an item that had none appends `keyword` as the item's last key. The note describes behavior the update path does not have.

Also (docs): docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:327-328 describes the schema `keyword` as "letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, at most 32 characters". The schema pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$` (TodoCatalog.schema.json `$defs/item.properties.keyword`, keywords.KEYWORD_RE) also requires a letter or digit first, so `_foo` or `-x` is refused. A project pinning its own schema copy from this note would get a looser pattern. todo-editor.md:185 states the rule correctly.

Also (system_shape): docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:329 says `add --spec`, the inbox drain and `inbox put --update` 'accept it and keep it right after the title'. add_items (`_item_fields`) and fill_keywords place it after `title`, but an update that sets `keyword` on an item without one goes through `item.update(...)` (updates.py:84), which appends the key at the end of the item; only `UPDATE_FIELDS` membership is tested (test_todo_sync_keyword_put.py:93-94).
fix: In updates._apply_one, place a newly set `keyword` right after `title` (reuse keywords._with_keyword when the item had none), and replace test_an_update_may_set_the_keyword with a behavioral test: apply_updates on MIN_CATALOG setting keyword on an item, then assert the value and that it follows `title`.
Or narrow the release note line in docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md to `add --spec` and the drain, and still make the update test call apply_updates and assert the stored value.

In updates._apply_one, when `keyword` is in fields and the item lacks one, rebuild the item with keywords._with_keyword before the remaining update; replace the constant check with a behavioral apply_updates test asserting the key follows `title`.
Drop `inbox put --update` from the 'keep it right after the title' clause in docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:329 and make the update test call apply_updates and assert the keyword lands.

Reword the line so only `add --spec` and the inbox drain keep it right after the title, e.g. "`add --spec` and the inbox drain accept it and keep it right after the title, and `inbox put --update` may set it (plan 2028)."
Or make updates._apply_one place a newly set `keyword` after `title` (reuse keywords._with_keyword) so the note holds as written.
Change the parenthetical to "letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 32 characters".
Reword the release note: add and the drain place it after the title; an update may set it.
Or place it: in updates._apply_one, when `keyword` is new to the item, rebuild the item with keywords._with_keyword-style ordering, and test the position.

minor.name: working-refs puts any catalog keyword string on the status line unchecked
minor.summary:
hide.ts keywordsIn (lines 57-66) accepts any non-empty string as a keyword. line.ts labelText and coloredLabel then write it verbatim into line.txt, line.json and the band-line atom. The schema's V1 pattern holds only for a catalog that passed `check`. A hand-edited catalog, or one on another checked-out branch, can carry a newline or an ESC sequence (OSC 8, SGR). That would split or corrupt the ccstatusline line and the fitCount length math, which assumes printable text.

Also (roast): keywordsIn accepts any non-empty string. The schema pattern only holds where a writer validated; a hand-edited or pinned-schema catalog with `keyword: "fix the\nthing"` or an embedded ESC sequence goes verbatim into line.txt (ccstatusline) and the band-line atom, where a newline splits the widget and an escape restyles the rest of the bar. The Python side already has the rule (KEYWORD_RE, KEYWORD_MAX); the reader drops it.

Also (tests): keywordsOf skips only non-string and empty keywords (hide.ts:63), and the tests at hide.test.ts:37-45 pin exactly that. A hand-edited or merged catalog keyword with a space, a 300-character string or an ESC sequence is accepted and statusText paints it raw into the ccstatusline output; the schema pattern (^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$, maxLength 32) is never enforced on the hook side and no test states the intended behavior.
fix: Mirror the V1 pattern and the 32-character cap in mirror.ts (for example KEYWORD_PATTERN and KEYWORD_MAX, pinned against TodoCatalog.schema.json by test_working_refs_contract.py), skip non-matching keywords in keywordsIn, and add a hide.test.ts case with a keyword holding '\n' or '\x1b'.

In hide.ts keywordsIn, skip a keyword that fails `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$/` or exceeds 32 characters (mirror both in mirror.ts and pin them to TodoCatalog.schema.json in tests/mods/test_working_refs_contract.py), and add a hide.test.ts case for a keyword with a space or an ESC.
Filter keywords in keywordsIn to the schema's pattern and length (mirrored like KEYWORD_KEY), and add hide.test.ts cases for 'two words', 'a'.repeat(33) and '\x1b[2J' being skipped.
Or, if raw pass-through is intended, add a line.test.ts case that documents it (at minimum strip control characters before painting).

minor.name: Exports that only tests use after the switch to catalogViewOf and drawRefs
minor.summary:
watch.ts now reads the catalog through catalogViewOf, and line.ts draws every ref through drawRefs. That leaves `retiredIdsOf` (its last production caller was readHide), the new `keywordsOf` and `formatRefs` referenced only from hide.test.ts and line.test.ts, so no production code path runs them.

Also (overall): watch.ts now reads the catalog only through catalogViewOf (watch.ts:401-402), and buildLine and statusText use drawRefs directly. That leaves three exports that no production code calls: retiredIdsOf (hide.ts:75), keywordsOf (hide.ts:81) and formatRefs (line.ts:74). They are tested as if they were the production path. A later change to catalogViewOf or drawRefs would pass these tests while the wrappers drift from what the line actually does.

Also (roast): watch.ts switched to catalogViewOf and buildLine/statusText call drawRefs directly, so `retiredIdsOf` (hide.ts:75), the new `keywordsOf` (hide.ts:81) and `formatRefs` (line.ts:74) have no production caller; only hide.test.ts and line.test.ts import them. They are dead wrappers that the tests keep green while the real path goes through other functions.

Also (system_shape): After this PR production code draws refs through `drawRefs`/`labelsOf` (line.ts buildLine, segmentOf, statusText) and reads the catalog through `catalogViewOf` (watch.ts readHide); no plugin calls `formatRefs` (line.ts:74), `retiredIdsOf` (hide.ts:75) or `keywordsOf` (hide.ts:81) any more. formatRefs' docstring still presents it as 'The refs as the line draws them', which the line no longer routes through.
fix: Remove retiredIdsOf, keywordsOf and formatRefs, and point their tests at catalogViewOf and buildLine (or an exported drawRefs).
Or keep them, but mark each one in its doc comment as a test-facing wrapper so a later reader does not look for a production caller.

Point the hide.test.ts retiredIdsOf and keywordsOf cases at catalogViewOf(...).retired and .keywords, then delete the two wrappers; keep formatRefs only if the doc comment says it is the plain-form helper the tests pin, or test buildLine(...).refs instead and drop it.
Delete keywordsOf and retiredIdsOf and point their hide.test.ts cases at catalogViewOf; delete formatRefs and test labelling through buildLine.
Keep formatRefs but have buildLine compute its own refs text through it, so the tested function is the one the line uses.
Route buildLine's own-refs text and segmentOf through formatRefs (or drop it and test drawRefs via buildLine), and drop retiredIdsOf/keywordsOf in favour of catalogViewOf in hide.test.ts.
Or mark them in their docstrings as test seams kept for the pure helpers.

minor.name: Cap-test comment misstates why the line collapses to +2
minor.summary: The comment at line.test.ts:259 says the unlabelled length (43) is 'too short for any labelled segment', but segment b alone fits: 'todo-k69m banner · [ b todo-zz99 ] +1' is 37 characters. The expectation 'todo-k69m banner +2' holds only because fitCount stops at the first segment that overflows (line.ts:127 `break`), so the test actually pins prefix-only fitting while its comment describes a different reason.
fix: Reword the comment to 'long enough for the whole unlabelled line, too short for the first labelled segment, and the cap never skips ahead to a later one'.
Or add a sibling assertion naming the prefix rule explicitly, so a future skip-and-continue cap fails with a clear reason.
